messages.subject: Modelling change in lavaan
parts:
Hello everyone!

In order to model mean differences, one can use growth function in lavaan. Now, I have found this presentation by Yves (http://www.personality-project.org/r/tutorials/summerschool.14/rosseel_sem_longitudinal.pdf). On page 37, he sets the first latent mean to zero and the second to one. Next, he examines whether there is a signifcant difference between time points. 

What is meant by baseline vs. difference according to latent means? How are "baseline" and the "difference" related to observed? 

Thanks for your help!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Modelling change in lavaan
parts:
On 12/01/2017 01:22 PM, 'Ahabsfriend' via lavaan wrote:
> On page 37, he sets the first latent mean to zero and the second to one.

No no. The first latent mean is 'fixed to zero', but the second one is
left 'free'. The syntax

posAffect2 ~ 1

simply refers to a latent mean, which is estimated freely. It is NOT
fixed to the constant 1.

> Next, he examines whether there is a signifcant difference between time
> points.
>
> What is meant by baseline vs. difference according to latent means? How
> are "baseline" and the "difference" related to observed?

The estimated latent mean for posAffect2 = -0.040, meaning that (on
average) children were -0.040 less positive on the 'posAffect' scale at
timepoint two. As the p-value is p = 0.106, we concluded that the
difference between the two time points (zero and -0.040) is NOT
significant.

Yves.
